lines.text: # T7d stub-jar additions — spec for oc-t4/cc-t3 to build the T7d adapter-mainline-stubs.jar
Scan of the U5 three-board hilog corpus (330 hilog files, ~1.77 GB, boards 5ea/5cd/61b, 2026-09-30..10-01)
plus 740 non-hilog evidence files (0 extra members). Base = `feat/bms-walls` `44ab7862e` (T7c stubs: tagsoup
/ MediaStore.*.EXTERNAL_CONTENT_URI). T7d adds the members below. Every method-level miss's log says
*"declaration … appears in …/adapter-mainline-stubs.jar"* → the class is already in the jar; add the member.
## Priority — FATAL misses fixable in adapter-mainline-stubs (add these)
| target app | class#member | signature | stub body | sev |
| **fd-gallery** | `android.provider.MediaStore#canManageMedia` | `(Landroid/content/Context;)Z` static | `return false;` (app takes the non-privileged path) | FATAL (main threw) |

| **fd-plus** | `android.graphics.ColorMatrix#setSaturation` | `(F)V` virtual | prefer the real AOSP saturation math (pure, no platform dep) if the stub holds the 4x5 array; else `{ /* no-op: clears resolution */ }` | FATAL |
| **wikipedia** | `android.net.ssl.SSLSockets` (NEW class) | 2 static methods | see below | FATAL (kills OkHttp Dispatcher → no network) |
// AndroidPlatform. isSupportedSocket=false makes OkHttp fall back to the standard SSLSocket path (no
// Android-specific TLS extensions) instead of crashing the Dispatcher thread. setUseSessionTickets is a
// no-op (session tickets are an optimization, not required for TLS to work).
public static boolean isSupportedSocket(javax.net.ssl.SSLSocket socket) { return false; }
public static void setUseSessionTickets(javax.net.ssl.SSLSocket socket, boolean useSessionTickets) {}
## Bonus — FATAL misses from other corpus apps (fold in if in scope)

| vlc | `android.net.ConnectivityManager#requestNetwork` | `(Landroid/net/NetworkRequest;Landroid/net/ConnectivityManager$NetworkCallback;)V` virtual | `{}` no-op (no network → callback never fires; app doesn't crash) |

| noice | `android.media.MediaFrameworkPlatformInitializer#getMediaServiceManager` | `()Landroid/media/MediaServiceManager;` static | `return new android.media.MediaServiceManager();` + NEW empty class `android/media/MediaServiceManager.java` (`public final class MediaServiceManager { public MediaServiceManager() {} }`). LOW priority — already CAUGHT (WESTLAKE-469), non-fatal. |

- `android.hardware.input.InputManagerGlobal#sService` — **29 apps** but the field lives in `framework.jar!classes2.dex`, not this jar, and it is a **CAUGHT** `[AdapterIIM]` reflection probe (info-level, process survives). Fixing it means patching framework.jar / the AdapterIIM shim, not the stub jar. Highest app-count but lowest value; leave it.

- `android.net.IConnectivityManager` — AIDL binder interface (Stub/Proxy/asInterface/txn codes), **not** a simple stub; currently caught by the Westlake local-service shim (`connectivity unavailable`, non-fatal). Leave to the shim.

- Out of scope (not android.*/java.*): `kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineStart` (caught by [COROUTINE-FIX]), conscrypt/Westlake keystore probes, `org.wikipedia.DefaultIcon` / logback (app/third-party classes).
## Honest coverage note — 2 of the 6 target apps are NOT stub-fixable
- **fd-libretube**: no android.*/java.* member blocker in the T7c run — only the caught `sService` probe. Its
remaining blocker (if any) is not an API resolution failure — look at conscrypt / native / UI, separately.
- **fd-feeder**: no android.*/java.* member blocker — only caught `sService` + out-of-scope
So T7d (stubs) can plausibly move **4 of the 6** targets past their API wall (wikipedia, fd-gallery, fd-plus,
x) + 2 bonus corpus apps (vlc, noice). fd-libretube/fd-feeder need a different track. Ground truth on board
1. **cc-t3/oc-t4**: apply the additions above onto `feat/bms-walls` mainline-stubs, build one
tree + turbine + d8), then re-gen the 27-file image with `t5_gen_image.sh` (dex2oat64 `ae865ddd`) = T7d
--oatdump scripts/lab/oatdump_remote.sh` (G1 image↔BCP + G2 suspend-check); gate-fail ⇒ no board.
3. **cc-wiki**: after G1/G2 pass AND 61b is released (watch the blackboard lock, do NOT grab it), LOCK 61b
≤30 min, package-deploy (27 image + T7d jar), run the 4 targets + vlc/noice + HW/ZZ/aegis/ooniprobe
controls, all `--reinstall`; rollback to U5 (resident byte-identical), UNLOCK.

- Stub edits applied to all 6 members (`t7d-stub-edits.patch`, on `feat/bms-walls` 44ab7862e base): ColorMatrix.setSaturation, MediaStore.canManageMedia, MediaStore$Files.getContentUri (`content://media/<vol>/file`), NetworkCapabilities.getSignalStrength, ConnectivityManager.requestNetwork, + new `android/net/ssl/SSLSockets.java`. 112 source files, uploaded to hw248 `/home/alvin/cc-wiki-t7d/src`.
- **Dropped MediaServiceManager / getMediaServiceManager** (noice bonus): `MediaServiceManager` is defined only in framework.jar, so adding it to the stubs jar would be a NEW shadow — G3 rejects it.

- **G3 built + tested** (`image_predeploy_gate.py --g3-*`): dex class-def map proves all 6 additions are safe — ColorMatrix/MediaStore/MediaStore$Files/NetworkCapabilities/ConnectivityManager are ALREADY in the stubs jar (adding methods, not classes); `SSLSockets` is defined in NO other BCP jar (new, no shadow). On THIS route-A board framework.jar does NOT define ColorMatrix (contrary to stock AOSP) — it is already a stub-jar class, so extending it is safe.
**BLOCKER — jar build needs FWK_TURBINE (framework-minus-apex), not on hw248:**

- The mainline-stub sources reference ~10 `@hide` framework types (`MediaServiceManager`, `StatsServiceManager`, `BluetoothServiceManager`, `NfcServiceManager`, `DeviceConfigServiceManager`, `TelephonyServiceManager`) + framework-internal annotations (`android.annotation.SystemApi/IntDef/RequiresPermission/NonNull/Nullable/CallbackExecutor`, `com.android.internal.annotations.*`). These live only in `framework-minus-apex` (the FWK_TURBINE interface jar), NOT in the SDK `android.jar` (javac against `prebuilts/sdk/current/system/android.jar` fails on all 10 + the annotations).

- FWK_TURBINE is absent from hw248 (`find` = none). The r16 tree `out/` is empty (no prior Soong build), so building it = a cold full-framework Soong build: hours, and hw248 is at **96% disk (44 GB free)** — a framework build risks filling a shared disk. Not run.
- oc-t4's T7c jar came from an environment that already has FWK_TURBINE built. That environment (not hw248) is where the mechanical compile belongs.

**Next (needs a decision):** (a) run the compile in the env that has FWK_TURBINE (oc-t4's), using the uploaded sources / this patch; or (b) point cc-wiki to a prebuilt framework-minus-apex.jar; or (c) authorize a cold `m framework-minus-apex` on hw248 despite the disk risk. Once the T7d jar exists: G3 → t5_gen_image.sh → G1/G2 → board 61b (after it frees).

# The "Compose blank-screen wall" — refuted by the T7d/5cd hilogs — cc-t3, 2026-10-01
**Ask (#80):** T7d/5cd left wikipedia, x, fd-noice alive-but-blank; the hypothesis (cc-wiki) was the
next wall is Jetpack Compose rendering (View apps light, Compose apps stay blank). Compare the blank
apps' hilogs to a lit View app; check lifecycle / AndroidComposeView attach / Surface / RenderThread
frame submission / swallowed exceptions; find a lit Compose app as a counterexample; propose a minimal
(cc-wiki's T7d/5cd run, fff8ef6ee). App child PID per app; counts scoped to that PID (system
## Verdict: it is NOT a Compose rendering wall
The blank/lit split does **not** correlate with Compose-vs-View at all, and every blank app already
| app | UI toolkit | T7d screenshot | decor childCount | app-PID frames | surface ops | Compose exc |
Four independent facts, each fatal to the hypothesis:
1. **A Compose app is lit.** `noice` and `fd-libretube` are Jetpack-Compose apps and both render their
own UI under T7d. The platform renders Compose. (Counterexample the ask requested.)
2. **A View app is blank.** `wikipedia` is a View/AppCompat app (decor child[0]=LinearLayout, childCount
=2, no ComposeView), yet it is blank — so "blank" is not caused by Compose.
3. **Same Compose app, opposite outcome, identical hilog.** `noice` (lit) and `fd-noice` (blank) are the
*same app* (com.github.ashutoshgngwr.noice) from two APKs. Their hilogs are indistinguishable:
decor childCount 1=1, app-PID RenderThread frames 4=4, surface ops 50≈49, `[COROUTINE-FIX]` failures
mLastLayoutFrame=Rect(0,0-1200,1920)`. If Compose rendering were the wall, both would be blank; the
render pipeline cannot be the differentiator because it is the same in both.
4. **Every blank app already renders.** Each reaches RESUMED, adds its window (`mAdded=true`,
`mFirst=false` = past the first traversal), measures the decor full-screen (1200×1920), obtains a
Surface, and submits RenderThread frames (app-PID frames 4–5, same as the lit apps). No blank app
logs a Compose failure — no `Recomposer` cancellation, no "Error captured", no `androidx.compose`
exception in its own stderr; the only exceptions are the universal benign shims (`[AdapterIIM]
sService`, `[COROUTINE-FIX]` field lookups) that lit apps log too.
`x` is a different category entirely: `[CHILD_CK] main_threw: RuntimeException: Unable to start activity
{com.twitter.android/com.twitter.x.lite.XL…}` — it crashes during activity start (0 surface, 1 frame),
it is not an alive-blank Compose case. It should be triaged as a crasher, not with wikipedia/fd-noice.
The apps draw a full-screen window and submit frames, but the pixels are not their expected content.
Because the render pipeline is identical between a lit and a blank instance of the *same* app, the
difference is **above** the platform render layer — it is app/APK/content, not a platform Compose gap:
- **Content emptiness / async load**: the first frames are a themed (often white) scaffold before the
app's content arrives (wikipedia's feed = network; a Compose onboarding that composes to an
effectively empty/white surface). Frames are white-on-white — real frames, no visible content.
- **Same-app APK divergence** (noice lit vs fd-noice blank): with identical runtime logs, the cause is
in the APK (the f-droid `fd-noice` build vs the direct `noice` build) or a deterministic first-screen
difference — not the platform. fd-noice is 3/3 blank, so it is deterministic, not timing jitter.
The hilog simply does not carry pixel content, so it cannot, by itself, decide "empty content" vs
"drawn but not composited to screen". That is what the on-board experiment must settle.
## Minimal on-board experiment plan (proposed, not run)
Cheap, single-board, one lock; targets wikipedia + fd-noice (blank) with noice + fd-gallery (lit)
as controls, all under the current unified state (U5 today; U6/U7 when adopted).
1. **Later settle** — capture t20/t40/t60 (not just 5,20) for wikipedia + fd-noice. If content appears
by t40/t60 → slow async content (network/DB), not a wall; if still blank at t60 → deterministic empty
content. (`bms_batch --shots 5,20,40,60` on those keys.) Cheapest first — rules "just slow" in/out.
2. **Deep view dump at t20** — `hidumper -s WindowManagerService -a '-a'` + a deep view-tree dump
(uitest `dumpLayout`) for a blank app. Distinguishes (a) content view has real children with non-zero
bounds + opaque background = drawn-but-not-composited, from (b) empty/transparent content tree =
nothing to show. The `[G2.14as-*]` probe only goes two levels; go deep here.
3. **Window visibility / z-order / alpha** — from the same `hidumper` WMS dump, confirm the blank app's
window is VISIBLE, alpha=1, top of z-order, not covered (SCBScreenLock / imehost). Rules out a
compositor-visibility cause (cf. RUNBOOK "黑屏先看 ZOrder").
4. **noice vs fd-noice, same board / same boot** — install and screenshot both back-to-back. Confirms
the same-app divergence is deterministic and APK-driven (not board/boot state). Pair with an offline
APK diff (dex + resources of the launch/onboarding path) to name the difference — this is the real
fix surface for fd-noice, and the template for the other f-droid-vs-direct blanks.
5. **Force redraw** — rotate or send the app background→foreground once, re-screenshot. If content
appears after an invalidate/recomposite, it is a first-frame/damage issue (a real, fixable platform
bug); if not, it is content. Distinguishes the last two hypotheses.
Route: the fix is per-app/per-APK (content load, or the f-droid build), not a platform "Compose
renderer". Do NOT open a Compose-rendering work item on this evidence. If (2)/(5) show drawn-but-not-
composited, that IS a platform bug — escalate then, with the deep dump as proof.
- **Benign-noise subtraction is canonical, not ad-hoc.** The exceptions I discount as "universal benign
shim noise" are the ones registered in `knowledge/gates/benign-log-signatures.json` (17 entries):
`class_linker` / `IFACE-BITS` / `VTLEN` E-lines are **not** app faults — they are appspawn-x's own
boot-time loader instrumentation on the root parent, excluded by scoping every count to the app child
- **first_fatal (cx-bms's `first_fatal.py` not yet on master → its rule applied manually:**
| **x** | `main_threw: RuntimeException: Unable to start activity {com.twitter.android/com.twitter.x.lite.XL…}` | **crasher — out of scope** |
So of the three the ask named, only wikipedia + fd-noice are actually alive-blank; **x is a crasher**
